items.title: The Day Mirror 1 Arrived!
items.caption:
It was 29 October 2025, and my first Magic Mirror had just arrived. Gemma and I unpacked it and couldn’t wait to try it. The mirror was exactly what I’d hoped for; the software wasn’t. It wasn’t terrible—it just wasn’t really anything, and it definitely wasn’t me.

So, I did what anyone would do: I started searching online for another program. Surely someone had already built exactly what I wanted? I found plenty of options, and some looked okay, but every one of them wanted another monthly subscription and none of them felt quite right.

At the time, I wasn’t thinking, “I’m going to build my own software.” I was thinking, “There has to be something out there that does exactly what I want.” I kept looking and looking until I eventually realised that I was describing a product that didn’t seem to exist.

At some point, I stopped searching for software and started making a list of everything I wished it could do. Then the list kept growing—not only with the things I already wanted, but also with ideas I hadn’t even known I wanted in a photo booth.

I never planned to build software. I never planned to build a website. I definitely never planned to spend the next nine months learning things I’d never even heard of—or creating an entire photo booth ecosystem.

I just couldn’t settle for “good enough.”

One idea became another.

Then another.

Then another.

Until one day…

Instapic existed.

Today, exactly nine months later, I’m proud.

Not because it’s finished…

(It probably never will be!)

But because an idea scribbled on a piece of paper somehow became something real. Something that didn’t exist before—and something that’s unmistakably me.

❤️ Lorie x
items.alt: Gemma and I posing together in front of our first Magic Mirror on the day it arrived.
